text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Open arms welcome if Malta decides to join the EU. The comment was made by the head of the Socialist group in the European Parliament, Pauline Green, when she started a visit to Malta on Wednesday. However, she said the group respected Malta's decision if it decided not to join the union. Green is to meet Prime Minister Alfred Sant and opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami.
- Bonn experts to help restore 17th century inn. The Auberge de Baviere built by the Knights of St John to house their peers from Bavaria, is in danger of collapse.

- Labour Party calls for inquiry into restoration project. The party said a unique, centuries old statue of Grand Master de Vilhena was severely harmed when it was moved under the Nationalist Party government to make way for an Independence Day monument.
- Malta woke up on Wednesday to unusually heavy mist that delayed some flights into Luqa airport by up to an hour.

- Request for more evidence in Raymond Caruana murder trial. Caruana was shot dead in a Nationalist Party club in December 1986, a few months before the Nationalist Party was elected for the first of two terms.
- Royal yacht Britannia due in Malta today. The yacht is here as part of British Culture Week.
